prompt: After `/drain`, the first pod showed `0/1` ready. What happened to it?
hint: Look at RESTARTS and at where the requests went.

choices.text: It was restarted with a clean state
choices.why: RESTARTS stayed at 0.

choices.text: It left the Service, and kept running
choices.why: Right. A readiness failure removes it from the endpoints and does nothing else.

choices.text: It was deleted and replaced by the ReplicaSet
choices.why: The same pod name was listed, still Running.

choices.text: It was moved to another node
choices.why: Pods never move; nothing about its node changed.

prompt: After the liveness probe restarted the broken pod, it was `1/1` ready again, although it had been drained. Why?
hint: What does a restarted container start from?

choices.text: Liveness overrides readiness
choices.why: Each probe decides its own consequence; neither overrides the other.

choices.text: The Service re-adds every pod after a restart
choices.why: The Service follows readiness answers, not restarts.

choices.text: Its new process never saw the drain
choices.why: Right. Both were in the old process's memory, and `/ready` answered 200 again.

choices.text: The kubelet skips readiness after a restart
choices.why: Readiness keeps being asked; it simply succeeded.

prompt: A team makes `/healthz` fail whenever the database is unreachable, and uses it as the liveness probe. The database goes down for two minutes. What happens?
hint: Which probe's consequence is a restart?

choices.text: Each pod leaves the Service until the database returns
choices.why: That is what a readiness probe would do; this is liveness.

choices.text: Nothing, since the pods themselves are healthy
choices.why: The probe says unhealthy, and the kubelet acts on the probe.

choices.text: Every copy restarts in a loop
choices.why: Right. Restarts cannot fix a database; the database belongs in readiness.

choices.text: The database is restarted by the shop's probe
choices.why: A probe only ever restarts the container it belongs to.

prompt: The pod `slow` needed thirty seconds to start and had only a liveness probe with `periodSeconds: 5` and `failureThreshold: 3`. Why did it never serve?

choices.text: It was killed after fifteen seconds, every time
choices.why: Right: three failures five seconds apart, long before it listened.

choices.text: The image was missing
choices.why: It ran and restarted three times.

choices.text: The readiness probe kept it out of the Service
choices.why: It had no readiness probe at all.

choices.text: Startup probes are on by default and failed
choices.why: There is no default startup probe.

prompt: Instead of a startup probe, a colleague proposes `initialDelaySeconds: 60` on the liveness probe. What does that cost?
hint: When would a real hang be noticed?

choices.text: Nothing: it is equivalent
choices.why: The delay applies to every start, and a fast start still waits a minute to be watched.

choices.text: The pod can never become ready
choices.why: Liveness does not decide readiness.

choices.text: Early hangs go unseen for a minute
choices.why: Right. A startup probe hands over to liveness at the first success instead of after a fixed wait.

choices.text: The kubelet refuses delays over thirty seconds
choices.why: There is no such limit.

prompt: Match each probe with what a failure does.
hint: The table at the end of the lesson.

pairs.right: Takes the pod out of the Service
Holds the other two until it succeeds

right_distractors: Moves the pod to another node

prompt: `slow-fixed`'s startup probe has `periodSeconds: 5` and `failureThreshold: 12`. How many seconds does the shop have to start before it is restarted?
A pod that fails its ___ probe is taken out of the Service's endpoints and keeps running.
hint: The question is: should it get traffic now?
